title: Cohort eviction and fidelity escalation manual
author: Lauren Chen
content:
Overview:

This document defines the cohort-driven eviction and fidelity-escalation strategy used by Redwood's serving runtime. It describes the architecture, kernel scheduling interactions, operational runbooks for incidents, and recommended profiling and benchmarking steps to validate policy changes. The guidance focuses on minimizing user-visible fidelity regressions while preserving SLOs for latency and availability.

Goals:
- Maintain 99th percentile latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes while maximizing throughput on cost-sensitive routes.
- Provide deterministic, observable escalation paths: eviction -> quantized fallback -> reduced-context variant -> full degrade to lower-cost model.
- Ensure safe, auditable rollouts of eviction/fidelity policies with canaries and automated rollback triggers.

Scope and components referenced:
- runtime-orchestrator: policy engine that maps requests to cohorts and routes.
- gpu-dispatcher: low-level kernel invoker and per-GPU slot allocator.
- kvcache-manager: session/KV cache lifecycle controller and warmstart hints.
- kernel-allocator: chooses kernel variants (e.g., fused-attn, tiled-attn, quantized path).
- fidelity-adapter: component that surfaces fidelity presets (max_tokens, sampling_temperature, context_prune).

Traffic cohorting model:
1) Cohort definition: requests are classified at ingress by route, customer-tier, and latency-sensitivity tag. Example cohorts:
   - realtime-high (interactive chat, enterprise, latency < 150ms goal)
   - batch-cost (embeddings, background rerank, throughput preferred)
   - degraded-tolerant (internal test, can tolerate reduced fidelity)

2) Cohort weights and priorities: Each cohort has numeric priority and eviction weight configured in the policy manifest. Higher priority prevents eviction; weights are used for proportional eviction during pressure.

3) Signal inputs: Eviction decisions use a sliding window of signals: GPU memory pressure, kernel queue backlog, tail latency (>95th), KV cache hit rate, and burst concurrency. These signals are normalized per-pool and reported to the runtime-orchestrator.

Kernel scheduling policy interaction:
- Kernel selection: kernel-allocator maps model + request cohort -> kernel variant. Preference order (by default): fused-opt -> tiled-opt -> quantized-path -> CPU-fallback. The allocator can be overridden per-cohort.
- Batch slicing: gpu-dispatcher slices batches with priority-aware buckets; realtime-high requests form a minimum-preserve slice to keep latency low.
- Hedging and speculative kernels: For cohorts marked "hedge-enabled", the runtime may launch a lightweight quantized kernel after timeout T_hedge_ms (default 40ms). First response wins; other kernels are cancelled.

Eviction and fidelity escalation ladder:
The ladder is a deterministic sequence a request can experience under resource pressure. Configurable at service-level in the policy manifest.
1) Soft eviction: drop queued low-priority requests before dispatch. Threshold: queue_length > Q_soft_threshold (default 250).
2) KV cache eviction: eject less-recent contexts from cache (policy: LRU with cohort weights). Trigger when cache_mem_util > 0.78.
3) Quantized runtime path: switch kernel variant to 8-bit or 4-bit quantized execution for eligible models. Trigger on node_mem_pressure or sustained tail latency > 2x SLO.
4) Context trimming: fidelity-adapter prunes non-critical tokens (system prompts or long histories) based on prune_policy.
5) Model variant swap: route to a smaller model variant with explicit fidelity delta recorded.
6) Slow-path fallback: route to dedicated lower-cost pool with higher latency but preserved throughput.
7) Circuit-break to return HTTP 503 for clearly out-of-budget requests after grace period.

Operational thresholds (recommended defaults):
| Metric | Normal | Soft-evict | Hard-evict | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GPU mem util | < 0.72 | 0.72 - 0.88 | > 0.92 | Use averaged 30s window |
| Kernel queue length | < 80 | 80 - 250 | > 250 | Per-dispatcher queue |
| KV cache hit rate | > 0.85 | 0.85 - 0.70 | < 0.70 | Consider cohort-weighted eviction |
| 95th latency | < SLO | > 1.5x SLO | > 2.5x SLO | SLO defined per-route |

Example policy manifest (YAML):

'''yaml
service: text-gen
cohorts:
  realtime-high:
    priority: 100
    preserve_min_slots: 2
    hedging: true
  batch-cost:
    priority: 40
    preserve_min_slots: 0
eviction_policy:
  kv_cache_watermarks: [0.6, 0.78, 0.92]
  soft_queue_threshold: 250
  hard_queue_threshold: 500
fidelity_presets:
  quantized_path: true
  prune_percentage: 0.2
rollout:
  canary_percent: 5
  rollback_on: [95th_latency > 2xSLO, error_rate > 1%]
'''

Note: replace triple single-quotes with code block markers in Confluence when rendering.

Profiling and benchmarking guidance:
- Bench environment: use the runtime-operational-simulator to mirror cohort mix. Always run new policy tests in a shadow cluster before canary.
- Benchmark steps:
  1. Create synthetic corpus representative of median and tail sequences (use sequence-length histogram from production).
  2. Run three experiments: baseline (no eviction), policy-on shadow, policy-on canary.
  3. Collect metrics: per-cohort 50/95/99 latency, kernel utilization, kernel-switch rate, kvcache hit rate, end-to-end error rate, token-cost delta.
  4. Validate fidelity by automated evals (prompt-sets tied to feature flags) to detect regressions > 2% BLEU/ROUGE or domain-appropriate metric.

Profiling playbook snippets:
- To capture a latency fingerprint for a cohort:
  - Enable cohort-trace on runtime-orchestrator for 10 minutes.
  - Collect GPU dispatch traces (gpu-dispatcher: /opt/runtime/bin/trace --cohort realtime-high --duration 600).
  - Run kernel heatmap extraction: /opt/runtime/tools/kernel-heatmap --trace-file traces.bin --output heatmap.png

- Useful commands:
  - runtimectl policy diff --service text-gen --from v2 --to v3
  - kvcachectl evict --cohort batch-cost --dry-run
  - gpuutil top --pool gpu-pool-1 --interval 10s

Runbook: incident triage (fidelity escalations causing customer impact)
1) Detect: Alert threshold triggers (95th latency > 2xSLO for > 3 minutes) -> SEV2.
2) Initial diagnostics (first 10 min):
   a) Check runtime-orchestrator decision log: /var/log/orch/decisions.log for last 15 min.
   b) Confirm kernel-switch rates: query telemetry: metric kernel_variant_switch{service="text-gen"}[5m].
   c) Check kvcache hit-rate: /metrics/kvcache/hit_rate by cohort.
3) Mitigation steps (order matters):
   1. Increase realtime-high preserve_min_slots by 1 via runtimectl: runtimectl set-cohort --service text-gen --cohort realtime-high --preserve_min_slots 3
   2. If queue backlog persists, temporarily raise soft-evict_threshold to reduce queued load: runtimectl set-eviction --service text-gen --soft_queue_threshold 320
   3. If tail latency still bad, toggle hedging off for batch-cost cohorts to reduce cross-kernel contention: runtimectl set-cohort --service text-gen --cohort batch-cost --hedging false
   4. As a last resort, flip fidelity flag to disable quantized path for sensitive tenants: runtimectl set-fidelity --service text-gen --cohort enterprise --quantized_path false
4) Post-incident: attach traces, kernel heatmaps, and a table of pre/post metrics to the incident ticket. Schedule a retro within 72 hours.

Rollback and safe deployment practices:
- Canary plan: 5% traffic to canary for 30 minutes with automatic escalation to 25% then 100% if rollup checks pass.
- Rollback triggers (automated): 95th latency increase > 1.5x baseline AND user-facing error rate increase > 0.5% OR fidelity eval regression > 2% on baseline prompt set.
- Safety nets: maintain a hot-path fallback pool (dedicated nodes that preserve previous runtime flags) to route canary traffic if model swap oscillation is detected.

Compatibility and release notes considerations:
- Any change that affects kernel-allocator mappings must include a compatibility table for model variants and quantization support. Example YAML excerpt in release notes:
  - model: meta-llama-2-13b
    supported_kernels: [fused-opt, tiled-opt, 8bit-quant]
  - model: small-rerank-3b
    supported_kernels: [tiled-opt, 4bit-quant]

- Note kernel ABI changes in release notes: if kernel op signature changes, annotate which runtime and gpu-dispatcher versions are incompatible.

Observability and dashboards to maintain:
- cohort-slo-overview: per-cohort latency and error SLOs.
- kernel-variant-switch-rate: heatmap by service and cohort.
- kvcache-watermarks: rolling 5m/30m hit-rate and evictions by cohort.
- fidelity-eval-regressions: continuous evals mapped to feature flags and cohorts.

Ownership and contact list:
- Oncall escalation: runtime-sre oncall -> eng-serving-runtime primary -> product-owner for route.
- Primary owners:
  - runtime-orchestrator: Miguel Santos
  - gpu-dispatcher & kernel-allocator: Tomás Rivera
  - kvcache-manager: Priya Nair
  - fidelity-adapter: Lauren Chen (author)

Appendix: quick checklists
- Pre-deploy policy change:
  1. Run shadow simulation with production traffic mix.
  2. Run fidelity eval suite and verify no regression > 2%.
  3. Verify observability dashboards created and thresholded for new metrics.
  4. Create rollout manifest with canary_percent and rollback_on policies.

- Emergency immediate mitigation cheat sheet:
  - runtimectl set-service-mode --service text-gen --mode conserve-memory
  - runtimectl disable-hedging --service text-gen --cohort batch-cost
  - kvcachectl bulk-evict --pool pool-a --percentage 10
